title: T-Count Study: 4 Gates
lesson: More non-Clifford gates can make useful checks harder to place.
brief: The mirror circuit now contains two T gates and two T† gates. The data circuit follows the same design family, but more positions constrain which Pauli checks are legal. Protect it with up to two checks.
learning_moment: Each T/T† site adds another point where a crossing check must be I or Z on that qubit. Useful X checks may still be placed on other spans, but some paths are no longer available. Compare Fidelity, Yield, and Cost with Puzzles 09a and 09b. Be careful with the conclusion: this experiment changes the circuit as well as the T count, so it shows how this family behaves under this noise model, not a universal law that Fidelity must fall with every T gate.
hint: Look at the T/T† sites first. Find where an X check would still be X when it reaches one. Then try a shorter or different span that stays legal. A check can start on two qubits.
reflection: Across the series, what changed in legal check placements, Fidelity, and Yield? What else changed besides T count?
noise_note: Most modeled errors are phase flips (Z errors).

noise.label: dephasing-dominated (Z-biased) level noise, same for the whole series

explanation: With four T and T† gates, an X check is blocked almost everywhere.
The last CNOT between q0 and q1 comes after every T gate, so a short check from slot 8, X on q0 and q1, can watch it for phase flips.
The other check, Z on q3 across the whole circuit, sees no phase flips at all. It helps another way: it ends at the readout, so it asks whether q3 is still 0 and catches readout flips on q3.
Together they just reach the target. Compare with Puzzles 09a and 09b.
